abstract: SHP2, a tyrosine phosphatase and key modulator of oncogenic signaling pathways, has emerged as a promising cancer target, but the impact of SHP2 mutations on therapy response remains unclear. Here we perform high-throughput mutagenic base editor screens in lung cancer cells to identify SHP2 mutations conferring resistance to migoprotafib and TNO155. Our screens identify numerous gain-of-function mutations associated with Noonan syndrome and various malignancies. Most resistance mutations overlap between inhibitors, although some exhibit elevated resistance to TNO155 compared to migoprotafib. Cross-referencing comprehensive genomic profiling data from predominantly advanced, SHP2 inhibitor-naive tumors reveals significant overlap between screen-enriched and tumor-associated mutations. We validate select mutations using in vitro and in cellulo assays and perform structural analyses to gain insights into the mechanisms driving resistance. Our study provides a comprehensive map of SHP2 mutations that reduce inhibitor sensitivity and identifies pre-existing variants that may confer intrinsic resistance to allosteric inhibitors in patients.
